text:
maya: Heads up — we're seeing a high-volume POST flood concentrated from a couple ASN blocks in SEA hitting /api/v1/generate. WAF alerts + 502s spiking. 90k req/min at edge, error rate ~18%. tagging @samir @security-oncall :red_circle:

samir: I'm on it, throttling policy applied to route /api/v1/generate -> temporary global rate-limit 20r/s per IP. pushing rule now.

ev an: logs look like this: `src_ip=103.45.210.3 method=POST path=/api/v1/generate status=502 ua="python-requests/2.31" bytes=512` repeating. many have sequential user-agents.

ekai: can we do geo-steering to route SEA traffic to a nullpool or slower path while we triage?

security-oncall: Yes, start with WAF block for the offending ASNs and a stricter per-IP burst/window. Also enable stricter connection rate on the edge proxies and enable logging -> audit stream. I'll open an incident ticket.

maya: Samir, share the exact rule you pushed. Ops-bot, post current edge metrics to the thread.

ops-bot: metric snapshot: requests_per_min=90000, 5xx_rate=18.1%, active_connections=12k, top_paths=["/api/v1/generate": 74%]

samir: pushed this as a temporary WAF custom rule (applied to edge cluster):

```
# block specific ASN ranges first-pass
SecRule REMOTE_ADDR "@ipMatchFromFile /etc/waf/blocked_asns_sea.txt" \\\\
  "phase:1,deny,status:429,id:100200,msg:'ASN block - high traffic',t:none"

# fallback: per-IP rate limit for the endpoint
SecRule REQUEST_URI "@beginsWith /api/v1/generate" \\\\
  "phase:2,chain,deny,status:429,id:100201,msg:'rate limit',t:none"
  SecRule TX:USER_RATE "@gt 20"
```

samir: also added an edge proxy directive: `max_concurrent=50` per source prefix.

evan: after applying ASN block + rate limits, request rate dropped to ~12k rpm and 5xx down to 3% in ~90s. good signal.

cs-liaison: A handful of paying customers reported elevated latencies around 12:01 UTC. I'll draft a brief notification: "We're mitigating an elevated traffic event affecting generation throughput; mitigations are active and we're monitoring."

security-oncall: Next steps: 1) keep ASN blocks for 4h then review, 2) add ASN list to blocked_asns_sea.txt source (ticket INF-7283), 3) increase audit logging retention for the spike window, 4) run a post-incident triage tomorrow AM to decide long-term WAF signatures / challenge flows (captcha / JS).

maya: Agree. Also need an action for engineering: instrument more fine-grained KV cache hits for the endpoint — if we can cache common prefixes we'll reduce cost during these bursts. Ticketing that to eng-runtime.

samir: note — false positives risk minimal since most traffic looks scripted: identical payload sizes and UA patterns. We'll preserve sample logs in S3 bucket `incidents/1800123456/` for forensics.

security-oncall: I'll annotate the incident with MITRE-ish labels and assign severity P2. Creating postmortem stub now.

maya: thanks all. keep this thread for updates. once stable we schedule a 30-min postmortem review and copy CS on final comms. :white_check_mark:
